historical_record.description: The Japanese Tea Garden dates from 1894; it has been determined eligible for the National Register of Historic Places.

Answering the Council for Civic Unity and a Board of Supervisors resolution, the Recreation and Park Commission recorded that it had no objection in principle to restoring the name "Japanese" Tea Garden to what was then the Oriental Tea Garden, provided the change cost its lessee nothing and had his consent.

Urged by the Consulate General of Japan and the Japanese American community, and noting the peace treaty with Japan, the Recreation and Park Commission unanimously voted to restore the name Japanese Tea Garden, to take effect on April 7, 1953, when the lease was renewed.

Asked by the California Historical Society and women's clubs, the Recreation and Park Commission directed that a memorial plaque to George Turner Marsh, who built the original tea garden for the Midwinter Fair, be designed for the Japanese Tea Garden and funded in the next year's budget.
